draft.title: Health of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
card: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have a lower life expectancy than other Australians. This difference is called a health gap.
The gap is not caused by culture or by individual choices. It is linked to the effects of colonisation, such as loss of land and disruption to communities.
Racism and unequal access to services also play a part. Services may be far away, costly or not culturally safe.
a health service run by the local Aboriginal community, for that community. These services lead much of the response, because they understand local needs and can offer care people trust.
draft.remember: The health gap is linked to colonisation, racism and unequal access, and community-controlled services lead much of the response.

a.q: Which statement best explains the lower life expectancy of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples?
opts: It is linked to colonisation, racism and unequal access
It is caused mainly by Aboriginal cultures and traditions
It results mainly from poor personal choices by individuals
It is a natural difference that no policy could change
a.why: The card links the gap to colonisation, racism and unequal access to services. Blaming individual choices is tempting, but the gap is tied to wider causes that individuals do not control.
a.clue: Look for a cause that sits outside any one person's control.

b.q: A remote town's Aboriginal community sets up its own clinic, run by a local board. Why do community-controlled services lead much of the response to the health gap?
opts: They know local needs and can offer care people trust
They replace the need for any other health services
They are the only services that can treat chronic disease
They remove the effects of colonisation on health
b.why: A service run by the community understands local needs and can offer care that people trust and use. It does not replace other services or undo the causes of the gap, so those options go too far.
b.clue: Think about who runs the service and what that means for trust.

a.best: It is linked to colonisation, racism and unequal access

b.best: They know local needs and can offer care people trust

problems.detail: "The gap is not caused by culture or by individual choices" is too absolute. AIHW estimates show health risk factors such as smoking account for part of the gap, about a fifth, while social determinants account for about a third. The accurate point is that behaviours play a part but are shaped by colonisation, racism and access, so they are not mainly personal choice. Suggested wording: "The gap is not caused by culture, and it is not mainly about individual choices."

Every wrong option is an absolute claim ("remove", "replace the need for any", "the only services"). The right option is the only hedged one ("can offer"), so a student can pick it without knowing the idea.

check.summary: Both questions are correct. However, the card says flatly that the gap is not caused by individual choices, when risk behaviours do contribute (shaped by wider causes). Also, in question b the right answer is the only option that is not an absolute claim, which gives it away.

b.q: A remote town's Aboriginal community sets up its own clinic, run by a local board. Why do services like this lead much of the response to the health gap?
